answer: Each verified identity must complete a challenge-bound voyage of T dependent modular squarings, where each result feeds the next. A Wesolowski proof makes verification compact but does not remove this sequential work. GPUs may run separate clones in parallel, yet cannot collapse one chain’s dependency or erase its elapsed time. Even with basalt and karst as challenge labels, each identity faces a physical delay, limiting rapid Sybil creation rather than making cloning impossible.
